Hydrogen direct injection: how tumble shapes the mixture

3D in-cylinder CFD of a direct-injection hydrogen engine in Simcenter STAR-CCM+, validated against published optical-engine measurements from Sandia National Laboratories, then used to quantify how intake tumble changes fuel–air mixing before ignition.

Simcenter STAR-CCM+In-cylinder RANS CFD Moving meshGaseous H2 injection PIV / PLIF validationPythonCAD preparation
01

The problem

Injecting hydrogen directly into the cylinder after the intake valves close prevents backfire and raises power density, but leaves very little time for mixing. Hydrogen's low density makes the jet strongly affected by the bulk charge motion. This project asks how much the intake-generated tumble changes the hydrogen distribution in the cylinder by the time of ignition.

02

Reference engine and data

The study uses the Engine Combustion Network (ECN) hydrogen engine at Sandia: a single-cylinder optical research engine with a four-valve pent-roof head and a centrally mounted single-hole injector. Its geometry and measured flow and fuel fields are public, so every CFD result can be checked against experiment.

04

Method

Full-cycle moving-mesh simulation from the exhaust stroke to compression TDC: multi-component gas (H2, O2, N2), realizable k–ε two-layer turbulence, coupled flow and energy. The choked 100 bar jet is represented by a notional nozzle so the near-nozzle shock cells need not be resolved. Validation compares tumble ratio, velocity fields and H2 mole fraction with the Sandia data for both tumble cases; the validated model is then run at additional tumble levels.

Mixture quality at ignition-relevant crank angles (−40 to −10 °CA) is measured by the mass-weighted uniformity index, the spread of equivalence ratio, the flammable mass fraction and the equivalence ratio near the spark location.

05

Results

Part A · Analysis of the measured data (complete)

Before running CFD, I processed Sandia's PLIF and PIV images (high tumble, 9 and 11 crank angles) in Python to set the targets the model has to hit. On the measurement plane, with a 4 mm band at each liner removed:

0.25 → 0.94Mixture uniformity index from 10° after injection (−130 °CA) to −30 °CA
−85 °CA99% of the plane is already flammable (φ ≥ 0.1); the rest of compression only evens out the mixture
×4 dropSpread of φ relative to its mean falls from 0.93 at −110 °CA to 0.23 at −70 °CA
Sign reversalThe in-plane tumble estimate swings strongly during injection and has reversed by −55 °CA: the jet dominates the intake-generated vortex

Part B · CFD validation and tumble sweep (in progress)

STAR-CCM+ simulations are being set up. CFD-versus-experiment comparisons and the tumble sweep will be added here when complete.
